topics.title: 课程作业
topics.summary: 在墨尔本大学，由各课程主管教师确定本课程及考核作业中生成式 AI 的使用边界；学生在将 AI 用于考核作业前须查验明确许可，且除获准情形外须独立完成提交作品。
topics.scope: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则修订框架（MPF1318 征求意见备忘录）及学生 IT M365 指引。

claims.text: Before using GenAI for assessment-related work, University of Melbourne students must check that their Subject Coordinator has authorised its use.

evidence.quote: Before you use GenAI for assessment-related work you must check to ensure that your Subject Coordinator has authorised its use.
evidence.title: GenAI at Melbourne (Academic Skills - Study Skills)
evidence.location: Section: Is it okay to use GenAI at Melbourne?; extracted text lines 6-6

claims.text: At the University of Melbourne, students are expected to produce their own perspective, experience, and knowledge in assessable work rather than rely on AI output alone.

evidence.quote: While GenAI can produce seemingly valuable or original output, your own perspective, experience and knowledge is what the University and future employers expect. Therefore, knowing what value you add is crucial.
evidence.title: GenAI at Melbourne (Academic Skills - Study Skills)
evidence.location: Section: Demonstrating Your Knowledge; extracted text lines 60-60

claims.text: Each University of Melbourne subject coordinator is responsible for setting out the bounds of appropriate GenAI use within their subject and having conversations with students for clarity.

evidence.quote: It follows that it is the responsibility of each subject coordinator to set out the bounds of appropriate GenAI use within their subject. Coordinators are strongly encouraged to consider possible use case scenarios for their assessments, set clear boundaries, and have conversations with their students to enable clarity about what tools are appropriate and for what tasks.
evidence.title: Generative AI in T&L at the University of Melbourne (Melbourne CSHE)
evidence.location: Section: Setting Subject Boundaries; extracted text lines 58-58

topics.title: 考试
topics.summary: 公开证据不足以确立全校统一的考试生成式 AI 允许规则。依据墨尔本大学防范 AI 规避的学习保障指引，在多数情况下要求受控安全考核（如现场监考考试）占课程总分至少 50%（2026–2028 年分步推进）；具体考试规则由各课程大纲规定，未经许可或未披露在考试中使用 AI 构成 MPF1310 学术不端，校内工具授权不代表考试许可。
topics.scope: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则修订框架（MPF1318 征求意见备忘录）及学生 IT M365 指引。

claims.text: Under University guidelines on assuring learning in the age of GenAI, in most cases subjects are designed so that secure assessment types account for at least 50% of total marks, with phased implementation (2026–2028) and programmatic exceptions.

evidence.quote:
In most cases, this means designing subjects so that “secure” assessments, in which learning
is assured, account for at least 50% of a subject’s mark (Principle 1).
evidence.title: Assuring Learning in the Age of GenAI: Guidelines and Principles for Assessment
evidence.location: Section: Assuring Learning Guidelines Principle 1; extracted text lines 10-11

topics.title: 披露声明
topics.summary: 墨尔本大学指引要求：凡在学业成果中直接引用或转述 AI 输出内容，必须在参考文献中规范标注出处；若用于头脑风暴、构思规划或润色编辑等过程性协助，须在作业末尾附具使用声明。
topics.scope: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则修订框架（MPF1318 征求意见备忘录）及学生 IT M365 指引。

claims.text: If students use an AI tool such as ChatGPT to generate output that is paraphrased or directly quoted in assessable writing, it must be cited and referenced as a source in the reference list.

evidence.quote: If you have used an AI tool or technology such as ChatGPT to generate an output which you either paraphrase or direct quote in your writing, you must cite and reference this output as a source in your reference list.
evidence.title: Academic Integrity at the University of Melbourne (Academic Skills)
evidence.location: Section: Citing AI Output in Reference List; extracted text lines 15-15

claims.text: University of Melbourne guidance distinguishes between citing AI output in the reference list when quoting or paraphrasing, and providing an acknowledgement declaration at the end of the assessment for other process uses like brainstorming, planning, or reviewing.

evidence.quote: If you have used an AI tool or technology in any other way (see below) in the process of completing your assessment, an acknowledgement of how you have used AI tools or technologies is required. You can create this acknowledgement by adding a declaration at the end of your assessment.
evidence.title: Academic Integrity at the University of Melbourne (Academic Skills)
evidence.location: Section: Acknowledging AI Tools (Declaration Requirement); extracted text lines 16-16

claims.text: At the University of Melbourne, using GenAI tools on an assessment task that does not permit them, or using them in preparation without acknowledgement, constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).

evidence.quote: It’s important your students realise that if an assessment task does not permit the use of such tools, or if they use such tools in the preparation of an assessment submission without acknowledgement, this constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).
evidence.title: Generative AI in T&L at the University of Melbourne (Melbourne CSHE)
evidence.location: Section: University policies in relation to Generative AI; extracted text lines 57-57

topics.title: 隐私与敏感数据
topics.summary: 学生与研究人员严禁向生成式 AI 工具上传姓名、出生日期、住址、机密敏感隐私信息或第三方版权材料。学校知识产权不得上传至外部平台；员工如需对教学材料进行 AI 审阅，建议使用校内 SparkAI。
topics.scope: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则修订框架（MPF1318 征求意见备忘录）及学生 IT M365 指引。

claims.text: University of Melbourne students must protect personal information and not upload full names, dates of birth, addresses, or other confidential, sensitive or private information to GenAI tools.

evidence.quote: Protect your personal information and that of others. Do not upload your full name, date of birth, address or other confidential, sensitive or private information.
evidence.title: GenAI at Melbourne (Academic Skills - Study Skills)
evidence.location: Section: Protecting Personal Information; extracted text lines 44-44

claims.text: When uploading material to an AI tool, University of Melbourne students must ensure they do not violate creator copyright without permission.

evidence.quote: When you upload this material to an AI tool, you may be violating the copyright of creators who have not given permission to do this with their material.
evidence.title: GenAI at Melbourne (Academic Skills - Study Skills)
evidence.location: Section: Respecting Copyright; extracted text lines 47-47

claims.text: Assessments and teaching materials constitute University IP and must never be tested on third-party external platforms like ChatGPT; testing or auditing must be done only within SparkAI or sanctioned platforms.

evidence.quote: Since assessments and other teaching materials constitute University IP, they should never be tested on third-party external platforms such as ChatGPT, since these platforms use all prompts and inputs to further train their models.  Any such testing/auditing must be done only within the University’s secure GenAI platform (SparkAI) or other University of Melbourne-sanctioned platforms.
evidence.title: Generative AI in T&L at the University of Melbourne (Melbourne CSHE)
evidence.location: Section: Protecting University Intellectual Property; extracted text lines 41-41

claims.text: Researchers are advised not to share confidential information or innovation details in generative AI prompts, as that may cause IP to no longer be owned by the researcher or University.

evidence.quote:
The University has advised researchers that they should
not share confidential information or information about an innovation  in a generative AI prompt, as that may mean
that the IP is no longer owned by the researcher or by the University.
evidence.title: University of Melbourne Submission: Inquiry into Generative AI in Education (July 2023)
evidence.location: Section: Inquiry Submission - Commercial IP and Confidentiality; extracted text lines 252-254

While students are allowed to use GenAI for study, all work submitted for assessment must follow the rules of the assessment and, if AI use is permitted, students must ensure this is acknowledged as described in Academic Integrity: unauthorised or undisclosed use of technology.

topics.title: 研究与成果出版

additionalTopics.title: 学术诚信与纪律程序
additionalTopics.summary: 依据 MPF1310，在考核作业中未经许可或未加披露使用技术构成学术不端。良好学术素养欠缺（Poor Academic Practice）被单列为由教师教育性纠正的非惩戒程序，与学院处理的一级不端及中央委员会审理的二级严重不端严格区分。Turnitin AI 检测报告仅作为核查线索而非违纪证据，MPF1323 设立 20 个大学工作日的申诉期。
additionalTopics.scope: 区分课程大纲具体规定、学生学术诚信制度（MPF1310）、学生申诉规定（MPF1323）、负责任科研行为准则修订框架（MPF1318 征求意见备忘录）及学生 IT M365 指引。

claims.text: At the University of Melbourne, using GenAI tools on an assessment task that does not permit them, or using them in preparation without acknowledgement, constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).

evidence.quote: It’s important your students realise that if an assessment task does not permit the use of such tools, or if they use such tools in the preparation of an assessment submission without acknowledgement, this constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).
evidence.title: Generative AI in T&L at the University of Melbourne (Melbourne CSHE)
evidence.location: Section: University policies in relation to Generative AI; extracted text lines 57-57

claims.text: The University of Melbourne academic misconduct framework explicitly categorizes unauthorized or undisclosed use of technology (including GenAI) as a breach type under academic integrity procedures.

evidence.quote:
Breach types
Plagiarism
Unauthorised re-use of previous work (self plagiarism)
Breach of examination or assessment rules or directions
Falsification or misrepresentation of data
Unauthorised or undisclosed use of technology (incl. GenAI)
evidence.title: Student Academic Integrity: What Changed in 2025? (MPF1310 Implementation)
evidence.location: Section: Managing Suspected Academic Misconduct - Breach Types; extracted text lines 128-133

claims.text: Poor academic practice refers to minor and unintentional departures managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, and is explicitly distinct from academic misconduct.

evidence.quote:
Poor academic practice refers to minor and unintentional departures from accepted scholarly conventions or failures to comply with assessment guidelines. Poor academic practice incidents are characterised by inexperience, lack of student knowledge, or poor academic skills, and does not compromise the purpose and/or integrity of the assessment.
Importantly, poor academic practice is not academic misconduct, may be treated as an assessment matter and managed within the marking and assessment guidelines set by the Board of Examiners for the subject.
evidence.title: Student Academic Integrity: What Changed in 2025? (MPF1310 Implementation)
evidence.location: Section: Poor Academic Practice Definition and Management; extracted text lines 66-67

claims.text: A high AI score in Turnitin's writing detection report is not proof of misconduct and does not on its own constitute grounds for making an allegation of academic misconduct.

evidence.quote: A high AI score in Turnitin’s writing detection report is not proof that academic misconduct has taken place (any more than would be the case when using the more familiar similarity report tool to flag potential plagiarism).  It does not, on its own, constitute grounds for making an allegation of academic misconduct.
evidence.title: Generative AI in T&L at the University of Melbourne (Melbourne CSHE)
evidence.location: Section: Turnitin Writing Detection Guidance; extracted text lines 37-37

claims.text: Turnitin AI detection results serve only as a prompt for further investigation; if suspected, students may be invited to explain their work and provide drafts or notes in an exploratory discussion.

evidence.quote:
As with the similarity report generated by Turnitin, the result of the AI writing detector tool is a prompt for further investigation.
Should there be a suspicion that part or all of your submitted assessment has been produced using generative AI, you may be asked to explain your essay and argument (how you developed the argument, what sources you used, how you reached the conclusion you did), or to provide drafts or notes of early versions of the assessment.
evidence.title: Advice for Students Regarding Turnitin and AI Writing Detection
evidence.location: Section: Advice for Students Regarding Turnitin - Prompt for investigation; extracted text lines 15-16

claims.text: Under University of Melbourne student appeals procedures, appeals against academic misconduct decisions must be submitted via the online form within 20 University business days from the original decision date.

evidence.quote: To submit an appeal, you must complete the online student appeals form within 20 University business days from the date of the original decision.
evidence.title: Academic Board: Student Appeals Guidance and Deadlines (MPF1323)
evidence.location: Section: Submitting an Appeal - 20 Business Days Window; extracted text lines 126-126

claims.text: Assuring student learning requires careful use of secure assessment types at key points where student authorship can be verified, contrasted with open assessments where rules may be circumvented.

evidence.quote: Assuring student learning requires the careful use of ‘secure’ assessment types at key points in the curriculum.
